title: Common-Sense Law Enforcement and Accountability Now in DC Act of 2025
official_title: To repeal the Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 enacted by the District of Columbia Council.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Clyde (R-GA) with 29 cosponsors; passed the Republican-majority House. In the Senate it would need 60 votes, and repealing a D.C. policing-and-justice-reform law is likely to draw unified Democratic opposition, making passage uncertain.
summary: Repeals a 2022 District of Columbia policing law, restoring the prior law as if that act had never been enacted.
brief: Repeals the D.C. Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 and revives the law it had changed.

top_lines.headline: D.C. Policing Law Repeal
subs: Repeals the D.C. Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022
Restores any law that act had amended or repealed
Uses Congress's authority over the District of Columbia

items.main: Names the Act the “Common-Sense Law Enforcement and Accountability Now in DC Act” (the “CLEAN DC Act”).
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Repeal of Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022

items.main: Repeals the D.C. Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 (D.C. Law 24-345).
items.detail: Any provision of law that the 2022 D.C. act amended or repealed is restored or revived as if that act had never been enacted. The bill exercises Congress's constitutional authority over the District of Columbia.

criticisms.why: Mr. Speaker, I strongly oppose this bill, which repeals the police accountability and transparency law that the District of Columbia enacted in 2023. Last year, violent crime in D.C. was down 35 percent, reaching an over 30-year low. This year, violent crime in D.C. is down 28 percent compared to the same period last year.

gaps: The bill repeals the 2022 D.C. policing act but does not enumerate which underlying laws are restored beyond directing that they revive as if the act had never passed.
It repeals the act outright but does not establish any replacement policing or accountability standard for the District.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Norton
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, I strongly oppose this bill, which repeals the police accountability and transparency law that the District of Columbia enacted in 2023. Last year, violent crime in D.C. was down 35 percent, reaching an over 30-year low. This year, violent crime in D.C. is down 28 percent compared to the same period last year.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Clyde
featured_quotes.text: If there is one thing that act doesn't do, it is create more justice. It creates injustice. The CLEAN DC Act is essential to restoring public safety in our Nation's Capital. For far too long, Washington, D.C., a city meant to embody freedom and prosperity, has been overwhelmed by violent crime. As millions of people visit D.C. every year, it is imperative that our Nation's Capital is safe for all residents and visitors. Yet, in recent years, this simply has not been the case.

modified: Restores any law the 2022 D.C. act had amended or repealed, as if that act had never been enacted
removed: Repeals the D.C. Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 (D.C. Law 24-345)

added: New exception: repeal does not apply to subtitle S of title I (sec. 5-365.01 et seq., D.C. Official Code)
New exception: repeal does not apply to subtitle A of title I (sec. 5-125.01 et seq. and sec. 5-302, D.C. Official Code)
modified: Full repeal narrowed to a partial repeal — Section 2 retitled "Repeal of Certain Provisions" and restructured into subsection (a) repeal plus subsection (b) exceptions
Short title updated to add the year: "Common-Sense Law Enforcement and Accountability Now in DC Act of 2025" / "CLEAN DC Act of 2025"
